rationale: The hypothesis posits that digital anomalies (specifically brachydactyly, 5th finger clinodactyly, or 2nd-3rd toe syndactyly) occur in approximately 50-70% of individuals with Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome (STISS) and serve as critical diagnostic discriminators. However, in the largest published cohort characterizing PSMD12 haploinsufficiency (Bézieau et al. 2022), 2-3 toe syndactyly was observed in only 5 of 24 individuals (20.8%), and overall extremity/skeletal findings exhibit high phenotypic variability. Furthermore, while 2-3 toe syndactyly, sandal gaps, and 5th finger clinodactyly do occur in individuals with 17q24.2-q24.3 microdeletions and PSMD12 variants (Hancarova et al. 2018, Feresin et al. 2025), these minor digital anomalies are non-specific and overlap extensively with conditions such as Dubowitz syndrome, Silver-Russell syndrome, and Nijmegen breakage syndrome, making them poor standalone discriminators without molecular or biochemical confirmation.

evidence.text: In an expanded cohort of 24 unrelated patients with Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome caused by PSMD12 truncating variants or copy-number deletions, 2 to 3 toe syndactyly was documented in only 5 patients (20.8%), demonstrating that this specific digital anomaly occurs at a substantially lower frequency than 50-70%.

source.quote: The expressivity of most clinical features in STISS is highly variable. In addition to previously reported DD/ID, speech delay, cardiac and renal anomalies, we also confirmed preaxial hand abnormalities as a feature of this syndrome. Of note, 5 individuals also showed 2 to 3 toe syndactyly.

evidence.text: Digital anomalies including tapered digits, fifth finger clinodactyly, large sandal gaps, and 2/3 toe syndactyly are observed in 17q24.2-q24.3 deletion cases encompassing PSMD12, but these exact features caused initial diagnostic confusion with Dubowitz, Silver-Russell, Nijmegen breakage, and Myhre syndromes.

evidence.text: Characterization of 6 individuals from two families with inherited truncating PSMD12 variants revealed variable skeletal manifestations and novel findings such as unilateral ectopic fingernail, highlighting marked inter- and intrafamilial variability rather than an invariant 50-70% presentation of specific classic digital defects.

conflicts: The hypothesis asserts a prevalence of 50-70% for brachydactyly/5th finger clinodactyly/2-3 toe syndactyly, whereas the largest systematic cohort study (Bézieau et al. 2022) found 2 to 3 toe syndactyly in only 5 of 24 individuals (20.8%).

The hypothesis claims these digital anomalies serve as a 'critical diagnostic discriminator', but literature on 17q24 deletions and PSMD12 alterations shows these exact features overlap broadly with and led to misclassification as Dubowitz, Silver-Russell, Nijmegen breakage, and Myhre syndromes.

new_directions.question_text: What is the sensitivity and specificity of the type I interferon-stimulated gene signature and mTORC1 remodeling in clinically discriminating STISS from overlapping syndromic neurodevelopmental disorders?
new_directions.rationale: Bézieau et al. (2022) identified an interferon gene signature and mTORC1/mitophagy remodeling as potential biochemical hallmarks for STISS, which may discriminate far better than overlapping physical anomalies.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true aggregate frequency of preaxial hand defects versus 2-3 toe syndactyly across all molecularly confirmed PSMD12 variants reported to date?
new_directions.rationale: Systematic pooling of all individual case reports and cohorts will establish accurate HPO frequencies and determine whether preaxial hand defects (e.g., thumb duplication/hypoplasia) offer higher specificity than toe syndactyly.
